geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the stepped mass into a terrace operation so the upper section reads as inhabitable public stepping rather than arbitrary tiers.
Lower the number of terrace levels to preserve a dominant primary mass and reduce the appearance of a stair object.
Keep the terrace effect but make it subtler so the silhouette remains continuous and capacity-bearing.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the arbitrary stepped mass emphasis with a more legible terrace-linked section that can support public ground logic and a coherent neighborhood edge.
Reduce the stair-like repetition so the upper mass reads as one calm continuous section rather than a generic tier stack.
Soften the stepbacks to preserve the dominant gesture while making the silhouette less code-like and more landform-like.
Moderate the bend to improve continuity and keep the body readable as a single mass instead of a sharply broken stack.

rationale: The candidate is coherently step-massed in multiple views, but the language is still primarily an arbitrary cascading pyramid rather than a neighborhood-living mass with a clearly active ground threshold and usable public void. The parcel appears contained, and the mass stays mostly within the boundary, but the access edge is not convincingly addressed: the thick blue frontage reads adjacent rather than opened to, so the public response is semantically weak. Across views the silhouette is readable, yet the stepped upper sections do not resolve into a convincing courtyard/terrace section tied to entry or shared ground. It is therefore only partially coherent as a massing diagram and does not hard-pass program fit for this brief.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a large central void and bridge-like upper connector can support a neighborhood/public program.

Stepped silhouette is coherent but not yet program-meaningful enough to count as a strong terrace section.
Keep the central mass anchor; do not fragment further.
